quantities.name: Mass
quantities.description: The quantity of matter in a substance, measured in kilograms.

quantities.name: Force
quantities.description: A push or pull on an object with a specific magnitude and direction; it can be represented by a vector.

quantities.name: Acceleration
quantities.description: The rate of change in velocity; the change in velocity over time.

quantities.name: Velocity
quantities.description: Displacement divided by the time over which the displacement occurs.

quantities.name: Displacement
quantities.description: The change in position of an object.

quantities.name: Time
quantities.description: Change, or the interval over which change occurs.

quantities.name: Energy
quantities.description: The ability to do work.

quantities.name: Work
quantities.description: The transfer of energy by a force that causes an object to be displaced; the product of the component of the force in the direction of the displacement and the magnitude of the displacement.

quantities.name: Power
quantities.description: The rate at which work is done.

quantities.name: Momentum
quantities.description: The product of mass and velocity.

quantities.name: Electric charge
quantities.description: A physical property of an object that causes it to be attracted toward or repelled from another charged object; each charged object generates and is influenced by a force called an electromagnetic force.

quantities.name: Electric current
quantities.description: The rate at which charge flows.

quantities.name: Acceleration Due to Gravity
quantities.description: The constant acceleration of a freely falling object, 9.81 m/s^2 near Earth's surface, independent of the object's mass.

quantities.name: Gravitational Constant
quantities.description: The proportionality constant in Newton's law of gravitation, the same everywhere in the universe.

quantities.name: Coulomb's Constant
quantities.description: The proportionality constant in Coulomb's law relating electrostatic force to charge and separation.

quantities.name: Radius
quantities.description: The straight-line distance from a center point, such as the center of a circular path or between two masses or charges.

quantities.name: Coefficient of Friction
quantities.description: A unitless number representing the ratio of friction force to normal force between two surfaces in contact.

quantities.name: Height
quantities.description: Vertical distance above a reference level, such as the ground.

quantities.name: Length
quantities.description: The measured extent of something from end to end.

quantities.name: Impulse
quantities.description: The average net external force on an object multiplied by the time the force acts, equal to the object's change in momentum.

quantities.name: Density
quantities.description: The mass per unit volume of a substance or object.

quantities.name: Volume
quantities.description: The amount of three-dimensional space occupied by a substance or object.

quantities.name: Area
quantities.description: The amount of two-dimensional space enclosed within a boundary.

quantities.name: Pressure
quantities.description: The force per unit perpendicular area applied to a surface.

quantities.name: Period
quantities.description: The time for one oscillation.

quantities.name: Frequency
quantities.description: The number of oscillations per unit time.

quantities.name: Wavelength
quantities.description: The distance between adjacent identical parts of a wave.

quantities.name: Voltage
quantities.description: The electric potential difference between two points, equal to the work done per unit charge moved between them.

quantities.name: Electrical Resistance
quantities.description: A material's opposition to the flow of electric current; for ohmic materials, the ratio of voltage to current.

quantities.name: Angular Velocity
quantities.description: The rate of change of an angle as an object rotates, equal to the rotation angle swept divided by the time it takes.

quantities.name: Spring Constant
quantities.description: A measure of a spring's stiffness, defined as the ratio of the force applied to a spring to the resulting displacement.

quantities.name: Angle
quantities.description: A measure of rotation or the amount of turn between two rays sharing an endpoint.

quantities.name: Angular Acceleration
quantities.description: The rate of change of angular velocity.

quantities.name: Torque
quantities.description: A measure of the twisting force that tends to cause rotation about an axis, equal to the product of a force and its lever arm.

quantities.name: Moment of Inertia
quantities.description: A rotating body's resistance to a change in its angular velocity, analogous to mass in linear motion, and dependent on how its mass is distributed about the axis.

quantities.name: Angular Momentum
quantities.description: A measure of a rotating object's tendency to keep rotating, equal to the product of its moment of inertia and angular velocity.

quantities.name: Drag Coefficient
quantities.description: A unitless number quantifying the drag or resistance of an object moving through a fluid, dependent on its shape.

quantities.name: Young's Modulus
quantities.description: A measure of a material's stiffness, defined as the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain along an axis.

quantities.name: Stress
quantities.description: The force per unit cross-sectional area within a material that arises from an applied load.

quantities.name: Strain
quantities.description: The fractional deformation of a material, defined as the change in length divided by the original length.

quantities.name: Temperature
quantities.description: A measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles in a substance.

quantities.name: Coefficient of Linear Expansion
quantities.description: A material-specific constant giving the fractional change in length per degree of temperature change.

quantities.name: Coefficient of Volume Expansion
quantities.description: A material-specific constant giving the fractional change in volume per degree of temperature change.

quantities.name: Boltzmann Constant
quantities.description: The proportionality constant relating the average kinetic energy of particles in a gas to its temperature.

quantities.name: Number of Particles
quantities.description: A count of discrete particles, such as molecules or atomic nuclei, with no associated unit.

quantities.name: Universal Gas Constant
quantities.description: The proportionality constant relating pressure, volume, amount, and temperature of an ideal gas, the same for every gas.

quantities.name: Amount of Substance
quantities.description: A count of elementary entities (atoms, molecules) in a sample, measured in moles.

quantities.name: Specific Heat
quantities.description: The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of one kilogram of a substance by one degree.

quantities.name: Latent Heat
quantities.description: The energy per unit mass absorbed or released when a substance changes phase at constant temperature.

quantities.name: Thermal Conductivity
quantities.description: A material's ability to conduct heat, defined as the rate of heat transfer through a unit thickness per unit temperature difference.

quantities.name: Stefan-Boltzmann Constant
quantities.description: The proportionality constant relating the power radiated by a black body to the fourth power of its temperature.

quantities.name: Emissivity
quantities.description: A unitless measure, between 0 and 1, of how effectively a surface radiates energy compared to an ideal black body.

quantities.name: Efficiency
quantities.description: The ratio of useful output to total input for a process, such as work output to energy input.

quantities.name: Linear Mass Density
quantities.description: The mass per unit length of a one-dimensional object, such as a string or rod.

quantities.name: Viscosity
quantities.description: A fluid's resistance to flow, relating the shear stress within it to the rate of shear strain.

quantities.name: Volume Flow Rate
quantities.description: The volume of fluid that passes through a cross-section per unit time.

quantities.name: Reynolds Number
quantities.description: A unitless number predicting whether fluid flow will be laminar or turbulent, based on the fluid's speed, density, viscosity, and the size of the flow.

quantities.name: Sound Intensity
quantities.description: The power carried by a sound wave per unit area.

quantities.name: Reference Sound Intensity
quantities.description: The standard reference intensity, roughly the faintest sound audible to humans, against which sound intensity levels in decibels are measured.

quantities.name: Sound Intensity Level
quantities.description: A logarithmic measure of sound intensity relative to a standard reference intensity, expressed in decibels.

quantities.name: Electric Field
quantities.description: The electric force per unit charge that would be exerted on a small positive test charge at a given point.

quantities.name: Capacitance
quantities.description: A conductor's ability to store charge per unit of electric potential difference across it.

quantities.name: Permittivity of Free Space
quantities.description: A physical constant describing how an electric field permeates a vacuum.

quantities.name: Resistivity
quantities.description: An intrinsic material property describing how strongly it opposes the flow of electric current.

quantities.name: Magnetic Field
quantities.description: A vector field describing the magnetic influence on moving electric charges, electric currents, and magnetic materials.

quantities.name: Permeability of Free Space
quantities.description: A physical constant describing the ability of a vacuum to support the formation of a magnetic field.

quantities.name: Inductance
quantities.description: A conductor's property of opposing a change in the current flowing through it, by inducing a voltage proportional to that rate of change.

quantities.name: Index of Refraction
quantities.description: A unitless ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to its speed in a given medium, describing how much the medium bends light.

quantities.name: Magnification
quantities.description: The ratio of an image's size (or apparent size) to the size of the object producing it.

quantities.name: Order Number
quantities.description: The integer counting which interference maximum or fringe is being described, in diffraction and interference patterns.

quantities.name: Speed of Light
quantities.description: The speed at which light and all other electromagnetic radiation travel in a vacuum, a universal physical constant.

quantities.name: Planck's Constant
quantities.description: The proportionality constant relating a photon's energy to its frequency, fundamental to quantum mechanics.

quantities.name: Decay Constant
quantities.description: The probability per unit time that a given radioactive nucleus will decay, characteristic of a particular isotope.

equations.name: Angular Displacement Under Constant Angular Acceleration
equations.description: Under constant angular acceleration, the angle swept grows with both the initial angular velocity and the acceleration, mirroring displacement under constant linear acceleration.

equations.name: Angular Frequency of a Mass on a Spring
equations.description: The natural angular frequency of a mass oscillating on a spring, set by the spring's stiffness and the mass attached to it.

equations.name: Angular Momentum
equations.description: A measure of a rotating body's tendency to keep spinning, equal to the product of its moment of inertia and angular velocity, conserved when no net external torque acts.

equations.name: Angular Velocity as a Function of Time
equations.description: Under constant angular acceleration, an object's angular velocity grows linearly with time, the rotational analog of velocity under constant linear acceleration.

equations.name: Linear Velocity from Angular Velocity
equations.description: A point at distance r from the axis of a rotating object moves at a linear (tangential) speed proportional to both the radius and the angular velocity, so doubling either one doubles the tangential speed.

equations.name: Arc Length from Rotation Angle
equations.description: The distance traveled along a circular path, equal to the radius times the angle swept, when the angle is measured in radians.

equations.name: Average Kinetic Energy of Gas Molecules
equations.description: The average translational kinetic energy of the molecules in an ideal gas depends only on the gas's absolute temperature, not on the type of molecule.

equations.name: Average Velocity
equations.description: Average velocity is displacement divided by the elapsed time; it depends only on where an object starts and ends, not on the details of how its speed changed along the way.

equations.name: Buoyant Force (Archimedes' Principle)
equations.description: An object submerged in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces.

equations.name: Capacitance
equations.description: A capacitor's capacitance is the amount of charge it stores per unit of voltage applied across it.

equations.name: Energy Stored in a Capacitor
equations.description: The electrical potential energy stored in a charged capacitor, which grows with the square of the voltage across it.

equations.name: Carnot Efficiency
equations.description: The maximum possible efficiency any heat engine can achieve operating between two temperatures, set purely by the ratio of the cold and hot reservoir temperatures.

equations.name: Centripetal Acceleration
equations.description: The acceleration of an object moving in uniform circular motion (resulting from a net external force).

equations.name: Centripetal Force
equations.description: Any net force that causes uniform circular motion is a centripetal force; it points toward the center of curvature, and its magnitude grows with mass and with the square of speed, but shrinks as the radius of the circle grows.

equations.name: Rate of Conductive Heat Transfer
equations.description: The rate at which heat conducts through a slab of material depends on the material's thermal conductivity, its cross-sectional area, the temperature difference across it, and inversely on its thickness.

equations.name: Conservation of Momentum in a Two-Body Collision
equations.description: In a collision between two bodies with no net external force, the total momentum before the collision equals the total momentum after, however it is redistributed between them.

equations.name: Equation of Continuity
equations.description: For an incompressible fluid flowing through a pipe of varying cross-section, the flow rate is the same everywhere, so the fluid speeds up where the pipe narrows.

equations.name: Coulomb's Law
equations.description: The electrostatic force between two point charges is directly proportional to the magnitude of each charge and inversely proportional to the square of the distance separating them; like charges repel and opposite charges attract, with the force acting along the line joining the two charges.

equations.name: Electric Current
equations.description: Electric current is the rate at which charge flows past a point in a circuit.

equations.name: De Broglie Wavelength
equations.description: Every moving particle has an associated wavelength inversely proportional to its momentum, revealing the wave nature of matter.

equations.name: Density
equations.description: The mass per unit volume of a substance or object.

equations.name: Displacement from Average Velocity Under Constant Acceleration
equations.description: Under constant acceleration, the average velocity over an interval equals the mean of the initial and final velocities, so displacement is just that mean multiplied by the elapsed time.

equations.name: Displacement Under Constant Acceleration
equations.description: Under constant acceleration, an object covers more distance in each successive interval of time, since it keeps speeding up as it moves. Displacement therefore grows faster than time itself.

equations.name: Double-Slit Interference
equations.description: Light passing through two closely-spaced slits produces bright fringes wherever the path difference between the slits is a whole number of wavelengths.

equations.name: Drag Force
equations.description: The resistive force a fluid exerts on an object moving through it, growing with the square of the object's speed.

equations.name: Efficiency
equations.description: The fraction of energy put into a system that comes out as useful work or output, rather than being lost, often to heat.

equations.name: Elastic Potential Energy
equations.description: The energy stored in a spring (or other elastic object) when it is stretched or compressed from its equilibrium position.

equations.name: Electric Field from Force per Charge
equations.description: The electric field at a point, defined operationally as the force a small positive test charge would feel there, divided by the size of that charge.

equations.name: Electric Field of a Point Charge
equations.description: The strength of the electric field surrounding a point charge, falling off with the square of the distance from it.

equations.name: Electric Potential Energy Between Two Charges
equations.description: The potential energy stored between two point charges, which decreases in magnitude as they're moved farther apart.

equations.name: Electric Power (Current and Resistance)
equations.description: The power dissipated by a resistor, expressed in terms of the current through it and its resistance, useful when the current is known but the voltage is not.

equations.name: Electric Power (Voltage and Resistance)
equations.description: The power dissipated by a resistor, expressed in terms of the voltage across it and its resistance, useful when the current is not directly known.

equations.name: Electric Power
equations.description: The rate at which electrical energy is supplied by a source or dissipated by a device; it is the product of current times voltage.

equations.name: First Law of Thermodynamics
equations.description: The change in a system's internal energy equals the heat added to it minus the work it does on its surroundings, an accounting statement of energy conservation.

equations.name: Volume Flow Rate
equations.description: The volume of fluid passing a cross-section of a pipe per unit time, equal to the cross-sectional area times the fluid's speed.

equations.name: Gravitational Potential Energy
equations.description: The energy an object has due to its position in a gravitational field, equal to the work done to raise it against gravity.

equations.name: Half-Life from Decay Constant
equations.description: The time it takes for half of a radioactive sample to decay, related inversely to the isotope's decay constant.

equations.name: Heat Transfer and Specific Heat
equations.description: The heat needed to change a substance's temperature depends on its mass, its specific heat, and the size of the temperature change.

equations.name: Hooke's Law
equations.description: The force needed to stretch or compress a spring by some distance from its equilibrium length is proportional to that distance, for deformations small enough that the spring remains elastic.

equations.name: Ideal Banking Angle
equations.description: The angle at which a curve must be banked so that a vehicle can round it at a given speed without relying on friction at all.

equations.name: Ideal Gas Law (Molecular Form)
equations.description: Relates the pressure, volume, and temperature of an ideal gas to the number of molecules it contains, via the Boltzmann constant.

equations.name: Ideal Gas Law (Molar Form)
equations.description: Relates the pressure, volume, and temperature of an ideal gas to the amount of gas present, measured in moles, via the universal gas constant.

equations.name: Impulse-Momentum Theorem
equations.description: The impulse on an object is equal to the average net external force acting on it multiplied by the time interval over which the force acts.

equations.name: Kepler's Third Law
equations.description: For a body orbiting a much larger central mass, the square of its orbital period is proportional to the cube of its orbital radius.

equations.name: Kinetic Energy
equations.description: The energy an object has by reason of its motion, equal to one-half its mass times the square of its speed.

equations.name: Kinetic Friction
equations.description: If two surfaces are in contact and moving relative to one another, then the friction between them is called kinetic friction. The kinetic friction force is proportional to the normal force pressing the surfaces together, scaled by the coefficient of kinetic friction.

equations.name: Heat of Phase Change
equations.description: The heat absorbed or released when a substance changes phase (melting, freezing, vaporizing, condensing) at constant temperature depends on its mass and its latent heat.

equations.name: Length Contraction
equations.description: An object moving at relativistic speed appears shortened along its direction of motion, as measured by an observer at rest.

equations.name: Linear Thermal Expansion
equations.description: A solid's length changes in proportion to its original length and the temperature change it undergoes, with the constant of proportionality depending on the material.

equations.name: Magnetic Field Around a Long Straight Wire
equations.description: The strength of the magnetic field circling a long, straight current-carrying wire falls off with distance from the wire.

equations.name: Magnetic Force on a Moving Charge
equations.description: A charged particle moving through a magnetic field feels a force proportional to its charge, speed, and the field strength, maximized when it moves perpendicular to the field.

equations.name: Magnetic Force on a Current-Carrying Wire
equations.description: A current-carrying wire in a magnetic field feels a force proportional to the current, the wire's length, and the field strength, maximized when the wire is perpendicular to the field.

equations.name: Magnification
equations.description: The ratio of an image's height to the object's height, related to how the image and object distances from the lens compare; a negative value indicates an inverted image.

equations.name: Mass-Energy Equivalence
equations.description: Mass and energy are interchangeable; the rest energy locked in an object's mass is that mass times the speed of light squared.

equations.name: Moment of Inertia of a Point Mass
equations.description: The rotational inertia of a single point mass revolving at a fixed distance from an axis, the building block for the moment of inertia of any rigid body.

equations.name: Linear Momentum
equations.description: The product of mass and velocity.

equations.name: Motional EMF
equations.description: A conducting rod moving through a magnetic field develops a voltage across its ends, proportional to the field strength, the rod's length, and its speed.

equations.name: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
equations.description: Every particle of mass in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that grows with the product of their masses and shrinks with the square of the distance between their centers.

equations.name: Newton's Second Law
equations.description: Net external force is proportional to and in the same direction as acceleration, and inversely proportional to mass.

equations.name: Ohm's Law
equations.description: An empirical relation stating that the current through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference across it, often written as I = V/R, where R is the resistance.

equations.name: Parallel Plate Capacitor
equations.description: The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor grows with the area of its plates and shrinks with the distance between them.

equations.name: Resistors in Parallel
equations.description: When resistors are connected across the same two points, the voltage across each is the same, and their combined resistance is found by adding the reciprocals of each.

equations.name: Pascal's Principle (Hydraulic Lift)
equations.description: A change in pressure applied to an enclosed, incompressible fluid is transmitted undiminished to every point in the fluid, letting a small input force produce a much larger output force over a larger area.

equations.name: Period-Frequency Relation
equations.description: Period and frequency describe the same oscillation from opposite ends, the time per cycle versus the number of cycles per unit time, so one is simply the reciprocal of the other.

equations.name: Photon Energy
equations.description: The energy carried by a single photon of light is proportional to its frequency, the relationship that launched quantum mechanics.

equations.name: Poiseuille's Law
equations.description: The flow rate of a viscous fluid through a cylindrical tube depends on the fourth power of the tube's radius, making even small changes in radius have a large effect on flow.

equations.name: Power
equations.description: The rate at which work is done.

equations.name: Pressure as a Function of Depth
equations.description: The pressure in a static fluid increases linearly with depth, as the weight of the fluid above adds to whatever pressure already exists at the surface.

equations.name: Pressure
equations.description: The force per unit area perpendicular to the force, over which the force acts.

equations.name: Range of a Projectile
equations.description: The horizontal distance a projectile launched and landing at the same height travels, which depends on its launch speed and angle above the horizontal.

equations.name: Stefan-Boltzmann Law of Radiation
equations.description: The power an object radiates due to its temperature grows with the fourth power of its absolute temperature, and depends on its surface area and emissivity.

equations.name: Radioactive Decay
equations.description: The number of undecayed radioactive nuclei in a sample shrinks exponentially with time, at a rate set by the isotope's decay constant.

equations.name: RC Time Constant
equations.description: The characteristic time scale over which a capacitor charges or discharges through a resistor, after which about 63% of the change has occurred.

equations.name: Relativistic Momentum
equations.description: At speeds approaching the speed of light, an object's momentum grows faster than mass times velocity, diverging as its speed approaches c.

equations.name: Relativistic Total Energy
equations.description: The total energy of a moving object, combining its rest energy and kinetic energy, which grows without bound as its speed approaches the speed of light.

equations.name: Resistance from Resistivity
equations.description: A wire's electrical resistance grows with its length and its material's intrinsic resistivity, and shrinks as its cross-sectional area increases.

equations.name: Reynolds Number
equations.description: A unitless number combining a fluid's speed, density, and viscosity with the size of the flow to predict whether the flow will be smooth (laminar) or chaotic (turbulent).

equations.name: Rotational Kinetic Energy
equations.description: The kinetic energy a rotating rigid body has due to its spin, the rotational analog of one-half mass times velocity squared.

equations.name: Rotational Power
equations.description: The rate at which a torque does work on a rotating body, the rotational analog of force times velocity.

equations.name: Rotational Work
equations.description: The work done by a constant torque acting through an angular displacement, the rotational analog of force times distance.

equations.name: Satellite Orbital Velocity
equations.description: The speed a satellite must maintain in a circular orbit at a given radius so that gravity supplies exactly the centripetal force needed.

equations.name: Resistors in Series
equations.description: When resistors are connected end to end in a single path, the same current flows through each, and their resistances simply add.

equations.name: Simple Pendulum Period
equations.description: For a mass swinging on a light string or wire, the period of oscillation depends only on the pendulum's length and the local acceleration due to gravity, not on the mass or the amplitude. This holds as an approximation for small displacement angles, less than about 15 degrees.

equations.name: Snell's Law
equations.description: When light crosses the boundary between two media, the angle it bends by is set by the ratio of the two media's indices of refraction.

equations.name: Sound Intensity Level
equations.description: A logarithmic scale, in decibels, comparing a sound's intensity to the faintest audible reference intensity, matching how loudness is actually perceived.

equations.name: Sound Intensity
equations.description: The power a sound wave carries per unit area, which determines how loud the sound is perceived to be.

equations.name: Period of a Mass on a Spring
equations.description: For a mass attached to a spring undergoing simple harmonic motion, the period of oscillation depends only on the mass and the spring's stiffness, not on the amplitude.

equations.name: Maximum Static Friction
equations.description: Static friction opposes the start of relative motion between two surfaces in contact and can increase to match an applied force up to a maximum, proportional to the normal force pressing the surfaces together.

equations.name: Thin Lens Equation
equations.description: Relates the distances from a thin lens (or curved mirror) to an object and its image to the lens's focal length.

equations.name: Time Dilation
equations.description: A moving clock runs slow compared to one at rest, by a factor depending on how close its speed is to the speed of light.

equations.name: Newton's Second Law for Rotation
equations.description: A net torque applied to a rigid body produces an angular acceleration inversely proportional to the body's moment of inertia, the rotational analog of F = ma.

equations.name: Torque on a Current Loop in a Magnetic Field
equations.description: A current-carrying coil placed in a magnetic field experiences a torque that tends to rotate it, the operating principle behind electric motors and galvanometers.

equations.name: Torque
equations.description: The rotating effect of a force applied at a distance from a pivot, maximized when the force is applied perpendicular to the lever arm.

equations.name: Transformer Equation
equations.description: An ideal transformer steps voltage up or down in the same ratio as the number of turns in its secondary coil compares to its primary coil.

equations.name: Velocity Squared Under Constant Acceleration
equations.description: Under constant acceleration, speed grows with distance traveled, but only as its square root, so covering four times the distance only doubles the speed gained.

equations.name: Velocity as a Function of Time
equations.description: Under constant acceleration, speed builds up steadily. Equal intervals of time always add the same amount of velocity, regardless of how fast the object is already moving.

equations.name: Voltage from Potential Energy per Charge
equations.description: Voltage, or electric potential, is defined as the electric potential energy per unit charge at a point in a circuit or field.

equations.name: Volume Thermal Expansion
equations.description: A substance's volume changes in proportion to its original volume and the temperature change it undergoes, with a coefficient roughly three times the linear expansion coefficient for solids.

equations.name: Wave Speed on a Stretched String
equations.description: The speed of a transverse wave traveling along a stretched string increases with the tension in the string and decreases with how much mass it has per unit length.

equations.name: Wave Speed
equations.description: The speed at which the disturbance moves. Also called the propagation velocity or propagation speed.

equations.name: Weight
equations.description: The weight of an object is defined as the force of gravity acting on an object of mass m. Near Earth's surface, where the only force acting on a freely falling object is gravity, this force equals the object's mass times the acceleration due to gravity.

equations.name: Work Done by a Constant Force
equations.description: The transfer of energy by a force that causes an object to be displaced; the product of the component of the force in the direction of the displacement and the magnitude of the displacement.

equations.name: Young's Modulus
equations.description: Relates the stress on a material to the strain it produces, for deformation along a single axis within the material's elastic range.
